triaged_this_lap.title: Eleven of the fourteen Fonts rows are silent no-ops through fillFromJson
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: The plan routes every settings row through api.settings.fillFromJson(json). AlphaTab 1.8.4's resources deserializer (RenderingResourcesSerializer.setProperty, alphaTab.core.mjs:29464-29508) has NO case for nine of the fourteen font names - they are deprecated getter/setter aliases over elementFonts - and effectFont + inlineFingeringFont are @json_ignore dead fields (alphaTab.d.ts:14617-14690). The reference gets away with it by assigning the live object directly, which hits the alias setter. The plan's architecture cannot.
triaged_this_lap.evidence: Ran against a real new Settings(): 'display.resources.titleFont NO-OP wrote bold 33px Georgia, still 32px' ... 62 applied, 11 silent no-ops. Dead: copyrightFont, titleFont, subTitleFont, wordsFont, effectFont, timerFont, directionsFont, fretboardNumberFont, barNumberFont, inlineFingeringFont, markerFont. Working: numberedNotationFont, tablatureFont, graceFont.
triaged_this_lap.before: | Display > Fonts | 14 | settings | display.resources. + copyrightFont, titleFont, ... markerFont |
triaged_this_lap.after: Re-key the nine alias rows onto display.resources.elementFonts.<EnumName>: copyrightFont->ScoreCopyright, titleFont->ScoreTitle, subTitleFont->ScoreSubTitle, wordsFont->ScoreWords, timerFont->EffectBeatTimer, directionsFont->EffectDirections, fretboardNumberFont->ChordDiagramFretboardNumbers, markerFont->EffectMarker, barNumberFont->BarNumber. effectFont and inlineFingeringFont have no elementFonts target AND are unread by the renderer.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Re-key nine rows to elementFonts; drop the two dead rows (group becomes 12, total 90) or ship them explicitly labelled inert.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: elementFonts is the only font route the 1.8.4 JSON serializer implements; verified fillFromJson({display:{resources:{elementFonts:{ScoreTitle:'bold 33px Georgia'}}}}) makes titleFont 33px.
triaged_this_lap.conflicts_with_decision: The maintainer decided every reference row ships. Dropping two rows touches that decision, so it is a real question, not a mechanical fix.

triaged_this_lap.title: A THIRD mis-bound reference row the plan does not flag: the wrong enum on the orientation row
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: The plan's Global Constraints say 'Do not port the fork's TWO mis-bound rows'. There are three. playground-settings.tsx:723-729 binds otherSystemsTrackNameOrientation but hands the dropdown the TrackNameMode enum (FullName|ShortName) instead of TrackNameOrientation (Horizontal|Vertical). The sibling row at :708-714 uses the correct enum, which is what makes it a slip. A porter told there are only two will mirror this one.
triaged_this_lap.evidence: sed -n '708,740p' on the reference shows enumType: alphaTab.model.TrackNameMode on the orientation row. Probed the live namespace: TrackNameOrientation = Horizontal|Vertical, TrackNameMode = FullName|ShortName - disjoint sets. A TrackNameMode name parses to undefined via JsonHelper.parseEnum.
triaged_this_lap.before: Do not port the fork's two mis-bound rows.
triaged_this_lap.after: Do not port the fork's three mis-bound rows. ... And its otherSystemsTrackNameOrientation row is offered with the TrackNameMode enum (FullName / ShortName) instead of TrackNameOrientation (Horizontal / Vertical); the row above it, firstSystemTrackNameOrientation, gets the right one.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Change 'two' to 'three', name the third, and annotate both orientation rows in the Step 1 inventory with model.TrackNameOrientation.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: Names the slip the plan's own count would otherwise hide, and pins the enum at the row so it cannot be guessed.

triaged_this_lap.title: The mix reset does not fire on the first score, does not cover volume, and is undone by playerReady
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: Three independent defects in one handler. (1) api.player is NULL on the first scoreLoaded: _onScoreLoaded triggers the event and only THEN builds the player (alphaTab.core.mjs:48025-48029); with EnabledAutomatic the constructor creates nothing while there is no score (:46684). So api.player?.resetChannelStates() silently no-ops on load one, and on a mode-changing load it reaches a player destroyed milliseconds later (:46690). (2) resetChannelStates() does NOT clear volume - it clears mute, solo and live transposition only (:38911-38917); mixVolume is initialised once per channel in _channelInit (:39222) and survives. (3) playerReady re-asserts every RENDERED track's channel volume to playbackInfo.volume/16 (:45587) with no fired-once latch, and each of the fourteen midi rows calls loadMidiForScore() -> midiLoaded -> readyForPlayback, so the sliders desync from the synth.
triaged_this_lap.after: Rebuild rows on scoreLoaded; do the ENGINE reset on playerReady (which fires after the player exists and re-fires on every swap and midi load), and re-assert each track's volume there too.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Move resetChannelStates() to a playerReady handler, and in the same handler push every row's current volume back through changeTrackVolume so AlphaTab's /16 re-assert cannot win.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: playerReady is the only event guaranteed to run after the player instance exists, and it is also the exact event that clobbers the volumes - so reacting there fixes the null-player hole and the desync with one handler.

triaged_this_lap.title: clearTrackTranspositions() cannot undo the carry-over it exists to fix
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: ModelUtils.applyPitchOffsets runs at the TOP of _internalRenderTracks (alphaTab.core.mjs:45837), i.e. BEFORE scoreLoaded fires, and stamps the stale transpositionPitches into the new score's staves. The plan then sets settings.notation.transpositionPitches = [] and calls updateSettings(), which re-runs applyPitchOffsets (:45686) - but with an empty array the loop body is never entered, so nothing is un-stamped. MidiFileGenerator then falls back to the staff value (:43020), so the next score is both DRAWN and PLAYED transposed by the previous score's offset.
triaged_this_lap.evidence: alphaTab.core.mjs:3691 (applyPitchOffsets loop is guarded by i < transpositionPitches.length), :45837, :45686, :43020.
triaged_this_lap.before: export function clearTrackTranspositions(api: AlphaTabApi): void;  // sets transpositionPitches = []
triaged_this_lap.after: Write a zero-filled array at least as long as the previous one - new Array(previousLength).fill(0) - so applyPitchOffsets actually re-stamps zero; or zero each staff.transpositionPitch directly.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Zero-fill rather than empty, and keep the previous length so every previously-transposed track is reached.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: applyPitchOffsets only touches track i when i < transpositionPitches.length; an empty array reaches no track, a zero-filled one reaches every track that was transposed.

triaged_this_lap.title: The e2e case the plan calls its proof of the reset cannot observe the reset
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: Global Constraints say of the reset: 'Established by reading the source, not by running - Task 7's e2e case is what proves it.' That case ('opening another score starts from a clean mix') asserts expect(await mutesAfterOpen()).toEqual([]) - the ABSENCE of replayed mutes, never the presence of a reset. And recordApiCalls wraps at[name] where at is the api itself; resetChannelStates lives on api.player, so the helper structurally cannot record it. The plan's only claimed proof of its own read-not-run item does not exist.
triaged_this_lap.before: expect(await mutesAfterOpen()).toEqual([]);  // + recordApiCalls(page, method) wrapping at[name]
triaged_this_lap.after: Teach recordApiCalls a dotted path ('player.resetChannelStates') so it can wrap a nested object, then assert the reset was called at least once after the new score is ready - and assert the audible consequence too (the previously muted channel is no longer muted).
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Extend recordApiCalls to resolve a dotted path, and add a positive assertion on the reset.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: Turns the plan's stated proof into a real one, and it is the same helper both popovers already use.

triaged_this_lap.title: The volume ratio is an absolute mix volume, so the slider at its own starting value is LOUDER than untouched
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: changeTrackVolume does not multiply anything: setChannelVolume assigns straight to the channel (alphaTab.core.mjs:40085 -> :38900 c.mixVolume = volume). AlphaTab's own baseline for that same slot is playbackInfo.volume/16 (:45590). So for a track the file sets to 12, the untouched mix volume is 0.75, but moving the slider to 12 - its own starting position - sends 12/12 = 1.0 and the track jumps LOUDER. The plan and the spec both call this 'a ratio against the level the file gives the track', which is not what the synth does.
triaged_this_lap.after: api.changeTrackVolume([track], row.fileVolume > 0 ? next / 16 : 0);  // OR keep the formula and record the jump as accepted v0 behaviour
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Either divide by 16 to match AlphaTab's own baseline so the slider starts neutral, or keep fork parity and state the jump explicitly in Notes and on the by-ear gate list.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: next/16 makes slider-at-file-volume reproduce exactly what AlphaTab set itself, so first touch is silent rather than a step up.
triaged_this_lap.note: The spec locks the ratio formula, so changing it is a Spec Delta - a real decision, not a mechanical fix.

triaged_this_lap.title: The state-telling tooltip decision does not land: bare names on both triggers, and no screen reader ever hears the state
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: Two halves. (1) The Global Constraint says 'The tooltip says the STATE, not just the name: Solo: on, not Solo' and lists the Settings gear and the Tracks trigger among the controls it covers - but Task 5's case asserts toHaveText('Settings') and Task 7's asserts toHaveText('Tracks'). (2) Base UI 1.6.0's Tooltip sets NO aria-describedby at all - there is no useRole anywhere in @base-ui/react/tooltip/, verified by rendering it (aria-describedby = null both nested and plain). So EVERY state-telling tooltip in this plan - Solo: on, Mute: off, Shown in the score - is invisible to a screen reader, and axe cannot flag it.
triaged_this_lap.after: Either exempt a trigger whose state is already carried by aria-expanded (and say so in the constraint), or give it a state ('Settings - closed'/'Settings - open'). And for every state-telling tooltip, carry the state in an announced attribute too: aria-pressed for Solo/Mute, or a stateful aria-label for the render-select box.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Add a Global Constraint sentence: a tooltip is decoration to assistive tech, so the state must ALSO ride on aria-pressed / aria-expanded / a stateful aria-label; and settle whether the two popover triggers are exempt from the state rule.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: Makes the maintainer's decision real for every user rather than only sighted mouse users, and removes the contradiction between the constraint and both tasks.

triaged_this_lap.title: EnabledExternalMedia is persisted and strands the transport with a misleading tooltip and an endless loading bar
triaged_this_lap.whats_wrong: player.playerMode ships all five PlayerMode options and is stored. Task 8 Step 4 builds a settled state for Disabled (playbackOff suppresses loadingPlayer and the Play tooltip reads 'Playback is turned off in Settings'). EnabledExternalMedia gets nothing: 'it needs no code of its own - the transport simply stays not-ready - but say in the PR that it is inert.' After a reload the drummer meets a permanently aria-disabled Play button whose tooltip still reads 'Play', with loadingPlayer true forever because only playbackOff suppresses it - the exact state Step 4 exists to prevent.
triaged_this_lap.before: const loadingPlayer = !failed && !playbackOff && (!playerReady || opening);   // + tooltip: playbackOff ? 'Playback is turned off in Settings' : playing ? 'Pause' : 'Play'
triaged_this_lap.after: Treat external media the same way as Disabled: a third settled state with its own tooltip ('This mode needs an external media player, which this app does not provide'), suppressing the loading bar; OR drop EnabledExternalMedia from the row's options.
triaged_this_lap.proposed_fix: Give external media a settled state and its own tooltip, or remove the option.
triaged_this_lap.why_it_works: Either way a persisted choice can never leave the player looking permanently broken with no explanation - which is the rule Step 4 already applies to Disabled.
triaged_this_lap.conflicts_with_decision: Dropping the option touches the maintainer's 'every setting ships' decision, so it is a real question.

defects.title: display.startBar and display.barCount need a redraw AND a MIDI regeneration
defects.detail: Both feed the engine's first/last-displayed-bar computation, used by the layout and by the sound generation. SettingApply is a three-way EXCLUSIVE union whose 'midi' branch returns before any redraw, so the schema cannot express these two rows. Symptom: the bar range redraws while the player keeps the sound built for the old range - cursor and playback land on the wrong bars, no error. Fix shape: add a fourth apply mode (push, regenerate, then redraw) and give both rows that value in the inventory table and the schema.

defects.title: On a normal page load the player can report itself turned off
defects.detail: readPlayer still runs on scoreLoaded, where actualPlayerMode starts at Disabled and is not resolved for EnabledAutomatic until a score exists. The same ordering makes a file swap report the OUTGOING player. Lap 1 moved the MIXER's reset to playerReady; this is Task 8's own read and is still on scoreLoaded. Fix shape: derive playbackOff from the app's own stored setting, and read the engine's actual player and readiness only from playerReady and from the mode write, clearing readiness on a score change.

defects.title: The Settings popover's metronome and count-in rows are not disabled while a recording plays
defects.detail: The transport disables its two buttons because the backing-track synthesizer ignores them; the popover edits the SAME two values a second time and never receives hasBackingTrack - confirmed absent from SettingsPopoverProps. The slider moves, the number changes, nothing is heard. Fix shape: pass the flag and disable those two rows with the mixer's existing unavailable-reason pattern.

defects.title: The by-eye human gate can pass without touching the row kinds most likely to be broken
defects.detail: It asks for one row per section across eight sections, over ~90 rows, so it can pass without touching a single sound-regenerating or stylesheet row - exactly where a wrong apply hides. Fix shape: walk one row per WAY-OF-TAKING-EFFECT and per row kind (one redraw, one push-only, one midi, one stylesheet, one api-property, both actions) and tick the criterion on that coverage.

defects.title: The 'no toJson' claim is true but misleading, and it is load-bearing
defects.detail: Settings has no instance toJson, but JsonConverter.settingsToJsObject DOES serialize settings. The claim is the stated reason an implementer would hand-transcribe 71 defaults (20 of them colour and font strings) out of a browser console. Fix shape: restate it accurately and replace the transcribe instruction with a co-located test asserting each shipped default equals what that converter reports for a fresh Settings().

defects.title: A mistyped enum option name is written as undefined and re-applied all session
defects.detail: JsonHelper.parseEnum returns undefined for an unrecognised name and the serializers assign it straight through. Because the whole document is pushed on every edit, that undefined is re-applied for the rest of the session. Neither guard catches it: the storage merge compares string to string, and the row gate walks names, not values. Fix shape: a validation helper that drops any value absent from its row's option list back to the shipped default, called before the restore push.

defects.title: The fourteen midi rows stop the music mid-song
defects.detail: loadMidiForScore is documented to stop playback and it resets the synthesizer. That contradicts 'neither popover blocks the player', which is the single reason v0 chose a popover. The non-blocking e2e case uses the zoom row, which takes the redraw path, so the lane never exercises the path that breaks the claim. Fix shape: say it in the constraints and the funnel comment, and scope the non-blocking promise to the redraw and push-only paths.

defects.title: Every reopen of Settings collapses all eight groups
defects.detail: The accordion sits directly inside the popover panel with no hoisted value, and the panel unmounts on close. With search deferred to v0.1 and ~90 rows behind eight similar headers, re-finding a group is a repeated cost. The mixer already solves the identical problem by keeping its state mounted. Fix shape: hold the open group ids above the panel.

defects.title: A failed export leaves the button looking clicked and says nothing
defects.detail: Neither export row has a try/catch or any success or failure signal. Every other failure path in this plan raises a Sonner toast; these two rows are the one place the pattern is missing. The successful path needs nothing - the browser's own download is the signal.

defects.title: Unticking the last drawn track does nothing and explains nothing
defects.detail: applyRendered guards against emptying the drawn set by returning before any state update, so the box never even flashes. Fix shape: render the last drawn track's box disabled with a tooltip saying at least one track must stay drawn - the unavailable-reason pattern already built for this.

open_questions_for_the_maintainer: Does 'every single setting' mean the reference panel's row set (what is built) or AlphaTab's whole settings document (two further groups, ~15 keys)? Worth settling BEFORE the by-eye gate rather than after it passes.
